{
  "jobspec": "#!/usr/bin/env bash

# Flux batch script (translated from LSF)

# LSF requested:
#   -J NET-seq
#   -o logs/snake_%J.out
#   -e logs/snake_%J.err

flux alloc \
  -n 1 \
  bash -lc '

mkdir -p logs

# Approximate LSF %J with Flux job id.
exec >"logs/snake_${FLUX_JOB_ID}.out" 2>"logs/snake_${FLUX_JOB_ID}.err"

# NOTE: LSF job name (-J NET-seq) is not expressed here as a portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but job identification in monitoring/accounting may be less clear.

set -o nounset -o pipefail -o errexit -x

module load fastqc
module load bowtie2
module load samtools
module load subread
module load gcc/7.4.0
module load R/4.0.3

# Function to run snakemake
run_snakemake() {
    local snake_file=$1
    local config_file=$2

    args='
        -oo {log.out} 
        -eo {log.err} 
        -J {params.job_name}
        -R "rusage[mem={params.memory}] span[hosts=1]"
        -n {threads} '

    # NOTE: This workflow uses Snakemake --drmaa with LSF-specific bsub arguments.
    # Flux does not provide a portable DRMAA+LSF layer, so these per-rule resource requests/logging directives
    # will not be honored under Flux.
    # Performance implication: jobs may run with wrong CPU/memory, may oversubscribe/underutilize resources,
    # and logging/placement controls per rule may be lost; you may need to reconfigure Snakemake to use a Flux
    # executor/profile or run locally within the allocation.

    snakemake -n \
        --snakefile $snake_file \
        --drmaa "$args" \
        --jobs 100 \
        --configfiles $config_file
}

# Run pipeline to process mNET-seq reads
pipe_dir=src/pipelines
samples=SAMPLES.yaml

snake=$pipe_dir/NETseq.snake
config=NETseq.yaml

run_snakemake $snake "$samples $config"

# Run pipeline to identify pause sites
snake=$pipe_dir/pauses.snake
config=pauses.yaml

run_snakemake $snake "$samples $config"
'

# Notes on omitted translations:
# - No LSF queue, walltime, CPU, memory directives were provided, so no Flux equivalents can be set.
#   Performance implication: the allocation will use site defaults, which may be insufficient.
"
}
